title: One-Pot Italian Potato Gnocchi with Sage and Ricotta
summary: Streamlined into a single pot, this Italian dumpling dish cooks light potato gnocchi directly in a fragrant emulsion of butter, vegetable broth, fresh sage, and crushed garlic. As the gnocchi cook, starch releases into the simmering broth, creating a creamy pan sauce without requiring separate boiling and draining steps. Whole milk ricotta and freshly grated pecorino cheese are folded in at the end, coating every pillow-soft dumpling in velvet richness. Tender baby spinach and lemon zest added right before serving provide bright acidity and color. This one-pot method reduces cleanup while maximizing flavor retention in every bite. Enjoy this comforting dinner hot with extra black pepper and toasted pine nuts. The starch-thickened butter sauce clings effortlessly to the light potato dumplings, proving that high-end Italian comfort food can be fast and clean.

steps.step: Place a deep, wide saute pan or Dutch oven on burner set to medium heat level.
Add pine nuts to dry pan, dry-toasting for three minutes until golden and fragrant.
Transfer toasted pine nuts to a small dish immediately to prevent scorching in pan.
Add extra virgin olive oil and two tablespoons of unsalted butter to hot pan.
Finely mince shallot and garlic cloves using chef knife on cutting board surface.
Add minced shallot and garlic to melted butter, cooking two minutes until softened.
Slap fresh sage leaves between hands to bruise, then add leaves directly into hot fat.
Fry sage leaves for two minutes until crisp and oil turns fragrant with sage essence.
Remove half of crisp sage leaves with fork and reserve for final meal garnishing.
Pour dry white wine into pan, scraping brown bits while wine simmers down for two minutes.
Stir in crushed red pepper flakes, grated nutmeg, garlic salt, and onion powder.
Dust one tablespoon flour over pan aromatics, cooking for one minute to form roux.
Slowly pour low-sodium vegetable broth into pan, whisking to dissolve flour smoothly.
Bring savory broth base to a lively simmer over medium burner flame setting.
Unpack fresh potato gnocchi and separate any dumplings that stick to each other.
Drop gnocchi directly into bubbling broth without boiling water in a separate pot.
Stir gnocchi gently with silicone spatula to ensure dumplings stay submerged in broth.
Cover pot with lid and cook for four minutes as gnocchi absorb liquid and swell.
Remove lid and check that gnocchi have floated to surface of simmering sauce base.
Observe as released potato starches naturally thicken simmer broth into silky sauce.
Add remaining unsalted butter and heavy cream into pot, stirring to enrich sauce.
Drop fresh baby spinach leaves into pot, folding leaves into hot sauce to wilt.
Season sauce with sea salt and coarsely ground black pepper according to taste preference.
Maintain gentle simmer for two minutes until spinach turns bright tender green.
Stir in fresh lemon juice to balance rich butter and starch profiles in pot broth.
Reduce burner heat to lowest setting so sauce stays warm without boiling dumplings.
Verify gnocchi texture is pillow-soft and tender without turning mushy or overcooked.
Prepare fresh cheese blend ingredients for final cream fold stage.
Grate pecorino romano cheese and fontina cheese using fine microplane tool.
Dollop whole milk ricotta cheese by tablespoons across surface of simmering gnocchi.
Stir grated pecorino and fontina cheeses gently into warm starch sauce until melted.
Fold ricotta partially into sauce, leaving creamy white swirls around potato dumplings.
Stir in fresh lemon zest and chopped basil leaves for instant herbaceous brightness.
Turn off burner completely and let pot sit covered on warm stove for two minutes.
Ladle one-pot dumplings and creamy cheese sauce into four shallow pasta bowls.
Top each bowl with reserved fried sage leaves for crunchy texture and visual interest.
Scatter toasted pine nuts over bowls to add nutty crunch against soft dumplings.
Garnish plates with extra chopped flat-leaf parsley and additional ground black pepper.
Drizzle remaining extra virgin olive oil over bowl rims just before serving guests.
Check that one-pot dish delivers piping heat and silky sauce coating every gnocchi.
Serve immediately alongside crusty Italian bread for wiping extra cheese sauce clean.
Enjoy rapid single-pot convenience with authentic Italian pasta house flavor.
